summary: Backend-only regression + targeted coverage for the analyze_image_for_quote / create_booking refactors. Authored /app/backend/tests/test_quote_booking_refactor.py with 7 tests covering: (a) full /api/quotes/image happy-path return contract, (b) non-image rejection, (c) image cache hit (same JPEG twice -> identical items/total + 2nd call meaningfully faster), (d) booking creation happy-path, (e) Friday weekday rejection (400), (f) slot-conflict path (after promoting seed booking to 'scheduled' via admin PATCH the duplicate slot returns 409), (g) unknown quote_id (404). Combined run against the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL: 57/57 PASSED — full prior regression (10 photo_reel_crop + 18 marketing + 15 push + 4 marketing_timezone + 3 push_health = 50) untouched plus 7 new refactor tests. Refactor preserves public signatures and return shapes — no observable behavior change detected.

minor.issue: _validate_pickup_request slot-conflict guard filters bookings by status {'scheduled','in_progress'} only. New bookings start in 'pending_payment'/'pending_customer_approval', so two consecutive customer bookings on the same Mon-Thu slot both succeed with 200 until an admin PATCHes the first to 'scheduled'. Confirmed via git history (commit 05354c4) this is intentional product behavior (only PAID bookings reserve slots) — but the review_request implies '409 on second booking' which is NOT the actual public-API contract. Pre-existing, NOT introduced by this PR; flagged for clarity.

Cache lookup is keyed on SHA-256 of the COMPRESSED 768px JPEG, not the original upload. Same source image with a different description still returns the cached items/total — meaning a customer's textual hint ('with stairs', 'heavy items') is silently ignored on cache hit. Pre-existing; surfaces only because the refactor isolated this behavior into a named helper.

action_items: (Doc/Clarify) Update review_request expectation for slot-conflict 409: it triggers only after an admin promotes the seed booking to 'scheduled'. If the intent is for two consecutive public bookings to clash, expand the status filter in _validate_pickup_request to include 'pending_payment'/'pending_customer_approval'.
(Optional) Consider keying the image cache on (image_hash, description_hash) so a different customer description re-runs the AI vision pass instead of returning the prior cached quote.
critical_code_review_comments: _resolve_user_id swallows ALL exceptions from get_current_user() and returns 'anonymous'. A malformed/expired token therefore silently downgrades the booking to anonymous instead of returning 401 — fine for 'token optional' design but worth a comment so future devs don't add 401-style assumptions on top of it.

_validate_pickup_request uses {'$regex': f'^{booking_data.pickup_date}'} on a string field. booking_data.pickup_date is user-supplied and unvalidated for regex metachars. If a caller submits 'a.*' as pickup_date, datetime.fromisoformat will raise first (mitigation), but it's still safer to switch to a $gte/$lt range query on the parsed datetime.isoformat() prefix or to re.escape() the value before injecting.

_compress_image_for_ai writes the compressed JPEG to image_path.rsplit('.',1)[0] + '_compressed.jpg' WITHOUT collision protection. Two near-simultaneous identical filenames (very unlikely with quote_<uuid> naming, but possible if a custom filename ever leaks into image_path) would race on the same temp path. Use NamedTemporaryFile(dir=...) instead.

_request_ai_vision_quote builds session_id=f'vision_{image_hash}'. Reusing the same session_id across calls with identical hashes can produce response coupling on Gemini's side; if the cache check fails for any reason (e.g. db.image_cache write failure) the next request will re-use the same conversation thread. Append an attempt counter or uuid suffix.

_send_post_booking_emails / _send_post_booking_sms are awaited sequentially after the insert. If either raises, the booking is already persisted but the customer never gets confirmation. Wrap each in try/except and log the failure (or move to BackgroundTasks) so a transient SES/Twilio outage doesn't bubble a 500 to the customer.

server.py is now 3865 lines and growing. The booking + quote helpers (~150 lines) plus the photo-reel module flagged in iter12 are obvious extraction candidates into routers/bookings.py and routers/quotes.py.

_parse_ai_quote_response uses re.search(r'\{.*\}', text, re.DOTALL) which is greedy and picks the OUTERMOST braces. If Gemini ever returns markdown with multiple JSON-looking blocks (e.g. ```json ... ``` followed by an explanation that includes '{...}'), the greedy match concatenates them and json.loads raises — falling through to _enhanced_text_fallback even though the response was valid. Switch to a non-greedy + balanced scan.
